newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 22.

text.p: PRAVO - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin repeated Russia's negative opinion on expanding NATO. Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and Chernomyrdin signed two documents yesterday, one to resolve Russia's debt from 1994 and the other an agreement for cooperation in the fight against organised crime.

- On Monday, the crown dropped to two percent below parity. The reason for this is probably the prognosis for the March trade balance, the approaching decisions to decrease interest rates and the tendency for foreign investors to leave the market.
- According to material which the Agriculture Ministry should present today, exclusively domestic investors should participate in the tender for an 89 percent stake in Becherovka.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - This Thursday, representatives of Trinecky Zelezarny, Skoda Plzen, ProWin, the English company Matallia International and the Liechtenstein company Blax Corporation will meet to discuss the possibilities for renewing operations in Poldi Steel. Blax bought the majority share in Poldi Steel last week for 4.3 billion crowns.

- In the next few days, representatives of the original Association for the Defence Industry (AOS), the head of RDP Group Viktoria Hradska and the former high military representative Karel Kuba will sign an agreement for cooperation with the French munitions association in hopes of getting a step ahead of the competitor Omnipol.
- Last year, leasing reached 46 billion crowns, giving the Czech Republic first place among post-communist countries and 12th place in Europe.
- Adamov a.s., the largest domestic manufacturer of polygraphic printing machines, is the first in the world to bring on the market new digital technology for printing in the A2 format.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Insurance company Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna decided to try its luck on the pension insurance market, despite the disapproval of several state officials. VZP bought a 51 percent stake in the pension fund Slavia from the brokerage Iceberg and changed the name to pension fund VZP.

- The Finance Ministry issued a fine of two million crowns on Moravskoceske Investicni Spolecnosti Ostrava, which has been under compulsory administration since March. The ministry also denied permission for the establishment of Delta Invest for not fulfilling the correct requirements.
- The management of Skoda Plzen dismissed the general director of Skoda Liaz, Josef Velisek, and placed Ross Roudnice in his place.

- With the prior approval of the central bank, the forced administrator of COOP Banka, Vladimir Medek, decided to increase the bank's basic capital by 500 million crowns by issuing shares worth 250,000 crowns.

LIDOVE NOVINY - It was calm at customs on the first day of the import deposit system. Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy announced after visiting customs that from April 28, all banks will be able to accept the import deposit.
- The Financial Administration for Prague 1 froze the bank account of the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) in Union Banka due to incomplete payment of pension taxes in 1991.

- Citizens' trust in President Vaclav Havel decreased in March to 66 percent from 87 percent in January, according to IVVM. Trust in the cabinet also dropped by five percent to 38 percent, and in parliament by two percent to 23 percent.

- The possibility that Prima Television will be taken over by Nova Television is met by negative reactions in the parliamentary commission for media, because this would mean the end of competition in Czech commercial television broadcasting.
